decisions.reason: As an established dental consumable line that fits the firm's core laboratory materials portfolio, it is likely to be retained unless demand has become too small to justify range complexity.
The PETG thermoforming blank remains close to the firm's established dental manufacturing business, so a large quality-focused supplier would usually keep it unless margin or volume underperform.
The UV-curing lacquer still complements the workflow offering, but its weaker strategic visibility and more peripheral role make it the most plausible candidate for portfolio pruning.

The intraoral contrast spray supports digital clinical and laboratory workflows that match the firm's direction, though it faces some risk if scanner compatibility or sales traction are weaker than expected.
